title: "The Gate to Longevity"
subtitle: Closed to many, but they'll still try their luck.

items.text: Go on, have a taste.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Who's there?

items.speaker: Reclining Lady
items.text: I was certain you'd been dying to try the clear soup, Mayfly.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Clear soup?
From the reflection in the bowl, Reed sees a frown on a face that doesn't belong to her. Through that reflection's eyes, she notices a white rim of sugar that rounds the bowl.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: You just poured a whole potful of sugar in, Paper Heron. You can hardly even call it clear soup anymore. Eugh, what a waste.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Aha, really? I think it could use a touch more.
Noise fills her head. Cold seeps through her clothes. Rough cloth rubs against her skin. The air spiced with the comfortable smell of wet dirt.

items.speaker: Boy I
items.text: *whining* Mama, my hands are cold.

items.speaker: Ancient Woman I
items.text: Cold or not, you don't press your hands against someone's neck! It's rude.

items.speaker: Ancient Man I
items.text: I'm visiting my cousin. Heard there will be something special at the fair this year.

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Classic Zhu snacks for only three wen! Only three wen!

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Zhu County? But, this looks totally different.
City Gate, Ancient Zhu County

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: You want more? Have you ... Have you lost your taste, Heron?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Not just my taste, all my senses. That's why I roam the land, see? I'm seeking a cure.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Then, you're here to see the immortal too?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Ah, no, merely seeking a companion of mine. She does have the look of an immortal, though I couldn't say for sure whether she is one.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But tell me about this immortal you seek.
Mayfly thinks for a moment, then continues shyly.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Honestly, I know very little about them. All I've heard is that an immortal is supposed to come to the fair this year to teach people the Method of Longevity.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: They say it grants both a long life and lasting health.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Its results are said to be remarkable. An old granny learned it, and now she can swim the Nanfei River back and forth, even during winter.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Maybe it's the cure you're looking for too!

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Sounds intriguing. I'll be sure to keep an eye out.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But why the hushed voice?
Mayfly looks around anxiously.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Because the guards might hear me. The magistrate posted a notice saying the rumor's false; anyone who spreads it will be punished.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Hmm, words do carry weight. Rumors can grow out of control if left unchecked.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: True.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Still, it's drawn all sorts to Zhu County. Just look at the line behind us. Some told me they came all the way from Liaodong, far in the frozen north.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Is that so? Good for them, eh?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Shhh! Keep your voice down. Aren't you afraid of the guards?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: You're a Daoist. They'll search you head to toe.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I heard all manner of folk are trying to sneak into the town, the kinds that'll do anything for the Method of Longevity.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: There've even been deaths. See those guards? They're checking every traveler looking for vagrants, Yao, and criminals. Speak of the Method, and you'll be locked away in an instant.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: That's why they're so strict. They've even got Reversion Bells to magically identify us Yao.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: But I think those things only work on the dull-witted ones. Quite a few have slipped through already.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Reversion Bells only reveal a Yao's true face. They cannot tell virtue from vice.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Yet there are things that can: truth potions, the Immortal's Brush, even some arcane beasts.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Hmm? You're not listening, Mayfly. Take a breath. All will be well.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Eugh, frost take me. I don't need a magic lesson right now.
Mayfly shakes her head, letting her gaze rest on Paper Heron's mule.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Hey, you've got a lot of stuff packed up on that mule. You selling those things at the fair?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: No, I wanted to get a gift for my friend, but I'm not so sure of her taste, so I bought whatever caught my eye. I'll let her choose whatever she likes.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Is this a snow lotus carving? Did you find it in the Western Regions?
Caught up in the excitement of this new sight, Mayfly can't help but start asking questions, her tone alive with interest.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: What was it like there? Is it as beautiful as they say? Please, tell me all about it.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Ah, the view was breathtaking. Standing at the cliff's edge, watching the world turn white with the falling snow. I didn't even realize where I was. My mule carried me there, see?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: The Western Regions, hmm, to the west, then? Where exactly is that?
Paper Heron's eyes dart upward, forward, side-to-side, until they look like a needle on a broken compass.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: *sigh*

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I almost forgot how hopeless you are with directions. Lucky I found you on your way here, or rather, on your way somewhere else entirely.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Never mind. Let's get back in line.
She doesn't wait for a response. Mayfly looks over the crowd toward the city gate, her fingers rubbing a hidden object in the folds of her clothes.
There's a low current of unease that runs through the crowd. As if they were moving along a treacherous bridge, each shift of their feet cautious as heads bob side-to-side, checking for movement.
It doesn't move. For a time, it feels like it has never moved at all. Each person taking their turn to sigh as they look ahead with a worried expression.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: *sigh* How much longer must we wait? I'll start growing roots if this line doesn't budge.

items.speaker: Ancient Man I
items.text: Move forward, will you?

items.speaker: Constable I
items.text: Get moving! Those who passed the cargo check must go to the Reversion Bell! Hurry it up. There's a whole line behind you!

items.speaker: Constable I
items.text: Next!
The impatient constable gestures for the static line to advance.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I'll be next.
Mayfly squeezes the little object tight beneath her robes as she edges forward.

items.speaker: Constable I
items.text: What's that you have tucked in your sleeve? It looks solid.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: N-Nothing, officer.

items.speaker: Constable I
items.text: Hands in the air. Give—
A cry comes from up ahead, causing both of them to turn their heads.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: What happened?
A bronze bell rings, its noise emanating from a man at the front of the line, the vibrations pressing him into the ground.

items.speaker: Civilian I
items.text: Aghh.

items.speaker: Civilian II
items.text: Claws. His hands are turning into claws!
Under the bell's power, the man transforms into a large yellow dog, its features fiendish, its fangs sharp.

items.speaker: Yellow Dog
items.text: *roar*

items.speaker: Civilian II
items.text: Run! It's a Yao! Run!

items.speaker: Constable II
items.text: Capture that monster! Don't let it get away!

items.speaker: Civilian III
items.text: Stop pushing! Someone fell down here!

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Hey. Stop-Stop pushing!

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Where's the Yao? Where?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Eight   views   merge,   the   mystery   of   Qi.   Three   lights   darken,   and   all   lose   their   way.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: W-What?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Heron, wh-what was that spell? I feel woozy.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Come on. Hop up.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: What's happening? I ...

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: We can't let that yellow dog tear through the crowd.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I'll subdue it before harm comes to anyone. Easy now, big fellow.

items.speaker: Yellow Dog
items.text: Roar!!!

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Ah, you're tougher than I thought.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Show me what you've got.
Who is responsible for this mayhem?

items.speaker: Yellow Dog
items.text: *whimper*
A young man in an officer's uniform knocks the yellow dog out with a single strike. As it crumples to the ground, he turns his blade toward Paper Heron now seated on her mule.
Causing chaos at the city gate, are we? Looking for trouble?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Your most discerning lordship, I swear on all that is good. 'Twas he who started it.
Hmph. Was there really any need for all this?
The officer's token hangs plainly and openly on his belt, tempting Paper Heron to begin reading its inscription aloud without thinking.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Patrol Bureau of Zhu County, Chief Constable, Chéng Héguāng.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: At your service.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Dù Liù, stay and maintain order. Yáng Wǔ, arrest this Daoist. Ensure she lifts the spell before you put her away. I will question her personally.

items.speaker: Du Liu & Yang Wu
items.text: Understood!
The spell's force lingers in the air. The others at the gate remain dazed as the world spins.
Dù Liù and Yáng Wǔ push their way through the confused crowd.

items.speaker: Civilian II
items.text: Aah. Where am I? Is this heaven?

items.speaker: Civilian III
items.text: Wait. What happened to the money in my purse? Did that dog curse my sight?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Ah, don't look at me. I didn't do anything.

items.speaker: Constable II
items.text: Damned yellow dog! You won't get away from us!
A dazed constable holds the Reversion Bell as he stumbles into the crowd.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Eh?
Under the bell's power, Mayfly's human form disappears.
In its place appears a wilting tuft of grass.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Oh, no!

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Wait, she's a ...?
Acting on pure instinct, Reed calls out, but the scene before her dissolves away like mist.
A light wind rustles her hair. Zhu County feels the first chill winds of autumn.
Without realizing it, she has left the gate tower and found herself walking alone through the dark streets.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: The wind can hold on to information for a long time, so I'm guessing that knot must've been here for ages. Then, that must have been Mayfly's memory?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Her true form was a tuft of reed, just like me.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: It was already winter, though; she would've been running out of time.
She thinks of the calendar in her notebook. Over three hundred boxes, two-thirds crossed out.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Then, my informant from the forum ... Could it be her?
